Overall, the district continues to demonstrate substantial compliance with applicable state and federal accessibility standards. However, the inspections identified a small number of recurring deficiencies, primarily related to door opening force, restroom signage, and path-of-travel obstructions. ---

**Section 3: District-Wide Recommendations**

The following recommendations are offered to the Board, the Superintendent, and school administrators based on the findings of the January and February 2026 inspections. These recommendations are organized by category and are intended to guide the district’s capital improvement planning, maintenance scheduling, and budget requests for the 2026–27 fiscal year.

---

**3.1 Door Openings and Hardware**

Manual door opening forces exceeding the 5 lbf maximum were the single most common deficiency noted across the district, appearing at eleven of the fourteen schools inspected. In most cases, the measured force fell between 5.5 and 7.0 lbf, indicating that the door closers are set too high or have drifted out of adjustment over time. The district should direct Maintenance & Operations (M&O) to perform a systematic adjustment of door closers at all school entrances, administrative offices, and restrooms. Where adjustment does not bring the force within the 5 lbf maximum, the closer should be replaced. This work can be completed by in-house staff and does not require outside contractors. The Accessibility Services Office (ASO) will re-test any door repaired under this recommendation within 60 days of the work order being closed.

The district should also adopt a standard specification for all new door hardware purchases: lever handles, no knobs; opening force not to exceed 5 lbf; and automatic door operators on all main public entrances. The current practice of installing manual doors at new construction sites has contributed to the recurring force violations.

---

**3.2 Drinking Fountains**

The inspection found drinking fountains with spout heights above the 36-inch maximum at six schools. In each case, the fountain was a wall-mounted unit with a manual push-button actuator. The district should prioritize replacement of these units with accessible, hands-free models. For the 2026–27 budget cycle, ASO recommends that the district allocate funds to replace at least four of the six non-compliant fountains, beginning with those located in gymnasium lobbies and student common areas where usage is highest. The remaining two fountains should be replaced in the following fiscal year.

While replacement is pending, M&O should post a temporary sign at each non-compliant fountain directing users to the nearest accessible fountain. The sign should include the location of the accessible unit and should be mounted at 48 to 60 inches above the floor.

---

**3.3 Restroom Facilities**

The most significant restroom issue identified during the inspections was at Lincoln Elementary School, where the accessible restroom in the kindergarten wing did not have a properly functioning emergency call button. The call button at that location was not connected to the main office and produced no signal when tested. This was classified as a Code 1 deficiency and was corrected on February 9, 2026, by M&O. The district should review the monthly testing log for all emergency call buttons to ensure that testing is actually being performed and documented. ASO recommends that the testing log be maintained at each school's main office and that the principal or designee initial the log after each monthly test.

The district should also evaluate the mounting height of toilet paper dispensers in accessible stalls. While the dispensers inspected were all within reach range, several were mounted at 24 inches above the floor, which is the minimum acceptable height but is not comfortable for all users. ASO recommends that new dispensers be mounted at 26 to 28 inches above the floor, and that M&O adjust existing dispensers when they are replaced.
**3.4 Drinking Fountains (continued) – Cedar Ridge Elementary School**

During the February 3, 2026 inspection of Cedar Ridge Elementary School, ASO staff reviewed the drinking fountains in all occupied wings and the gymnasium lobby. The school has a total of eight drinking fountains. Six are accessible units with both a standard and a lower-height basin. Two are older wall-mounted units with a single basin and a manual push-button actuator.

The two single-basin units are located in the gymnasium lobby and in the corridor outside the music room. Both units have the basin rim mounted at 34 inches above the floor, which is within the required reach range. However, the push-button actuator on the gymnasium lobby unit requires 6.5 pounds of force to activate, exceeding the 5-pound maximum permitted under the current standards. The actuator on the music room unit requires 5.25 pounds of force, also above the maximum. Both units were classified as Code 2 deficiencies because they do not prevent use of the facility, but they do not provide equal access for all users.

The remaining six fountains, including the accessible units in the kindergarten wing and the upper-grade corridor, were found to be in compliance. The accessible units have a clear floor space of 30 inches by 48 inches in front of the basin, and the basin rim is mounted at 32 to 34 inches above the floor. The push-button actuators on these units require 3 to 4 pounds of force and are mounted on the front of the basin. No temporary signage was needed at Cedar Ridge because the two non-compliant units are located within 50 feet of a compliant accessible unit in the same corridor or lobby.

M&O has been issued a work order to adjust the actuator tension on both single-basin units. The work order, M&O-2026-0317, was created on February 5, 2026, and is scheduled for completion by February 27, 2026. If the actuator cannot be adjusted to fall within the 5-pound maximum, the units should be replaced with hands-free models. ASO will re-inspect both locations after the work order is marked complete.

**3.5 Parking and Passenger Loading Zones – Cedar Ridge Elementary School**

The parking lot at Cedar Ridge Elementary School has 142 standard parking spaces and 6 accessible spaces. The accessible spaces are located at the north end of the lot, adjacent to the main entrance walkway. All six accessible spaces have the required 8-foot access aisle, and the access aisles are marked with blue paint and the international symbol of accessibility. The surface of the lot is asphalt and was found to be in good condition, with no cracks or potholes that would impede travel.

The van-accessible space at the north end of the lot has a 5-foot vertical clearance, which is below the 8-foot 2-inch minimum required for van-accessible spaces. The clearance is limited by the branch of a mature oak tree that overhangs the space. This was classified as a Code 2 deficiency. The tree is maintained by the Grounds Department, and ASO has requested that the branch be pruned to provide the required clearance. The pruning is scheduled to be completed by March 15, 2026, before the spring planting season begins.

The other five accessible spaces have no vertical clearance issues. The access aisle for each of these spaces is flush with the parking surface and connects directly to the curb ramp. The curb ramp at the north end of the lot has a slope of 1:12 and a flared side with a slope of 1:10, both within the acceptable range. The ramp surface is concrete with a broom finish and was found to be free of cracks and chips.
**3.6 Gymnasium and Elevator – Westbrook Middle School**

The gymnasium at Westbrook Middle School is the primary indoor physical education facility for the school and is also used for community events after hours. The gymnasium has two main public entrances: one at the east side, off the main corridor, and one at the west side, adjacent to the locker rooms. Both entrances are equipped with double doors. The east entrance has a power-operated door opener on the left leaf, which was tested during the inspection and found to be functioning within the required 5-second opening and closing cycle. The west entrance has no power-operated opener; the door is a manual double set with a combined opening force of 8.5 pounds, which exceeds the 5-pound maximum for interior doors. This was classified as a Code 2 deficiency. M&O has been issued a work order, M&O-2026-0341, created on February 10, 2026, to install a power-operated door opener on the west entrance. The work order is scheduled for completion by March 20, 2026. ASO will re-inspect the west entrance after the work order is marked complete.

Inside the gymnasium, the main floor is a hardwood surface with a slip-resistant finish. The surface was found to be in good condition, with no warping, splinters, or uneven transitions. The basketball court lines are painted and in good condition. The gymnasium also has a stage at the north end, which is used for assemblies and performances. The stage is elevated 24 inches above the gymnasium floor. There is no ramp or lift providing access to the stage. The only means of access is a stairway with three steps at the west side of the stage. The stairway has a handrail on one side, which is within the required height range of 34 to 38 inches. The lack of an accessible route to the stage was classified as a Code 1 deficiency, as the stage is a program area that must be accessible. ASO has recommended that a portable ramp be acquired and stored in the gymnasium equipment room. The ramp should have a slope of 1:12 or less and a minimum clear width of 36 inches. A request for quote has been sent to three vendors, and ASO expects to have a recommendation by March 5, 2026.

The gymnasium also has a public address system and a scoreboard mounted on the east wall. The scoreboard controls are located at the scorer's table, which is at floor level and accessible. The PA system controls are in a locked cabinet at the north end of the gymnasium, behind the stage. The cabinet is at a height of 48 inches above the floor, which is within the accessible reach range of 15 to 48 inches. The cabinet lock was operable with a standard key, and the controls were found to be in good working order.

The elevator at Westbrook Middle School is located in the main lobby, adjacent to the school office. The elevator provides access to all three floors of the building. The elevator car has a clear width of 42 inches and a clear depth of 54 inches, which meets the minimum dimensions for a standard accessible elevator. The car door has a clear opening of 36 inches. The elevator was inspected on February 12, 2026. The car leveling was tested and found to be within 0.5 inches of the floor landing at all three stops. The door opening and closing time was measured at 4 seconds, which is within the required range. The elevator car has a handrail on the back wall, which is mounted at a height of 34 inches. The handrail is in good condition, with no loose or missing brackets.

**General**

Northgate High School is a two-story building constructed in 1972, with a single-story science wing added in 1988 and a gymnasium addition completed in 1995. The main building houses administrative offices, classrooms, the library, and the cafeteria on the first floor, with additional classrooms and the music department on the second floor. The science wing is connected to the main building by an enclosed corridor at the east end of the first floor. The gymnasium is located at the west end of the campus and is connected to the main building by an outdoor walkway.

The campus has a total of 1,847 students enrolled, of whom 23 receive special education services. The school has one full-time nurse, one counselor, and two assistant principals. The main office is located on the first floor of the main building, directly inside the main entrance.

**Parking and Exterior Routes**

The main parking lot is located on the north side of the campus, with 212 spaces, including 8 designated accessible spaces. Of these, 4 are van-accessible with an 8-foot aisle. The accessible spaces are located closest to the main entrance, and the access aisle for the van-accessible spaces is on the passenger side. The surface of the parking lot is asphalt, and the accessible spaces are marked with the International Symbol of Accessibility and a "Van Accessible" sign. The signs are mounted on posts at the front of each space, and the bottom of the signs is at a height of 60 inches above the ground. The slope of the parking lot surface in the accessible spaces is 1.5%, which is within the maximum allowable slope of 2%. The accessible route from the parking lot to the main entrance is a sidewalk with a width of 48 inches. The sidewalk has a cross slope of 1%, and the surface is in good condition, with no cracks or heaving noted. The route passes through a gate in the perimeter fence, which has a clear opening of 36 inches. The gate is a double gate, and the accessible route passes through the left leaf. The gate is not self-closing, but it is held open by a hook and eye latch during school hours. The latch is at a height of 42 inches above the ground.

The main entrance has a vestibule with two sets of doors. The outer doors are a pair of aluminum frame and glass doors, each with a clear opening of 34 inches when one leaf is open. The inner doors are also a pair, with a clear opening of 34 inches. The doors have lever handles, and the opening force was measured at 6 pounds, which is within the allowable maximum of 5 pounds for interior doors but exceeds the 5-pound limit for exterior doors. The door closer on the outer set was noted to be out of adjustment, causing the door to close with excessive force. The closer was adjusted by M&O staff on the day of the inspection, and the opening force was re-measured at 4.5 pounds. The vestibule has a clear floor space of 6 feet by 6 feet, which is sufficient for maneuvering. The threshold at the exterior doors is 0.5 inches high, and the threshold at the interior doors is flush with the floor.

**Main Building – First Floor**

The corridor leading from the lobby to the east is 72 inches wide, with a floor surface of vinyl tile. The corridor is free of obstructions, and the doors along the corridor have lever handles. The classrooms along the corridor have door openings with a clear width of 32 inches. The classroom doors have a threshold of 0.5 inches, which is within the allowable maximum of 0.5 inches for interior doors. The door opening force was measured at 4 pounds for a sample of 5 doors.
**Summary of District-Wide Compliance Status**

The 2026 annual accessibility inspections covered all 23 schools in the Fairview Unified School District, including 15 elementary schools, 5 middle schools, and 3 high schools. Inspections were conducted between January 5 and February 27, 2026, by the Accessibility Services Office (ASO) with support from Maintenance and Operations (M&O) staff. This report presents the findings of those inspections and outlines the actions required to bring each facility into compliance with applicable accessibility standards.

**Overall Compliance Rating**

Of the 23 schools inspected, 6 were found to be in substantial compliance, with only minor deficiencies that were corrected on site or scheduled for routine maintenance. Eleven schools were found to be in partial compliance, with one or more deficiencies requiring corrective action. Six schools were found to be in significant non-compliance, with multiple deficiencies that require more extensive remediation. None of the schools were found to be in full compliance with all applicable standards, and no school was found to be so deficient as to require immediate closure or relocation of programs.

The most common deficiencies identified across the district were:

- Exterior door opening force exceeding the 5-pound maximum (found at 14 schools)
- Ramp slopes exceeding the 2% maximum (found at 9 schools)
- Missing or incorrect signage, including Braille and raised characters (found at 11 schools)
- Restroom grab bar installation issues (found at 8 schools)
- Parking space signage or access aisle issues (found at 7 schools)

**Status of Corrective Actions**

As of the date of this report, a total of 47 work orders have been generated to address deficiencies identified during the 2026 inspections. Of these, 23 have been completed, 14 are in progress, and 10 are scheduled to begin within the next 30 days. The ASO will track the completion of these work orders and conduct follow-up inspections at each school once all identified deficiencies have been addressed.

documents.title: Fairview Unified School District Accessibility Compliance Report – 2026
documents.content:
**To:** Board of Education, Superintendent's Cabinet
**From:** Accessibility Services Office (ASO)
**Date:** January 15, 2026
**Re:** District-wide accessibility compliance findings and recommendations

---

**EXECUTIVE SUMMARY**

The Accessibility Services Office (ASO) conducted its annual accessibility compliance inspections at all 34 district school sites between January 5 and February 6, 2026. This report summarizes findings from those inspections and provides recommendations for corrective action during the 2026–27 fiscal year.

Overall, the district continues to demonstrate substantial compliance with applicable state and federal accessibility standards. However, the inspections identified a small number of recurring deficiencies, primarily related to door opening force, restroom signage, and path-of-travel obstructions. These findings are detailed by school in the attached appendix.

The district's accessibility compliance report for the 2026 inspection cycle is issued as of the date above. The findings and recommendations in this document reflect the condition of facilities at the time of inspection and are considered current as of issuance.

---

**INSPECTION SCOPE AND METHODOLOGY**

Inspections were conducted by ASO-certified accessibility specialists using the 2010 ADA Standards for Accessible Design and the California Building Code (Title 24, Part 2) as reference standards. Each school site was evaluated for compliance in the following categories:

Accessibility Services Office issued_accessibility_compliance_report_on 2026-01-15 date. Record status: current.

- Accessible parking and passenger loading zones
- Exterior routes and ramps
- Entrance and interior doorways
- Restrooms and drinking fountains
- Signage and wayfinding
- Emergency egress and areas of rescue assistance
- Classroom and assembly area accessibility
- Playground and outdoor recreation areas

A total of 34 sites were inspected. Each site received a site-specific inspection report, which was provided to the principal and facilities staff. Deficiencies were coded by severity and required action:

- **Code 1 – Priority:** Immediate safety hazard or barrier to program access. Corrective action required within 30 days.
- **Code 2 – Standard:** Non-compliant condition that does not pose an immediate hazard. Corrective action required within 180 days.
- **Code 3 – Observation:** Condition that is compliant but warrants monitoring or planned maintenance.

---

**DISTRICT-WIDE FINDINGS**

The following summary represents aggregate findings across all inspected sites.

| Deficiency Category | Code 1 | Code 2 | Code 3 |
|---------------------|--------|--------|--------|
| Parking and passenger loading | 0 | 3 | 2 |
| Exterior routes and ramps | 1 | 6 | 4 |
| Entrances and doorways | 2 | 9 | 7 |
| Restrooms | 0 | 12 | 5 |
| Drinking fountains | 0 | 4 | 3 |
| Signage | 0 | 8 | 6 |
| Emergency egress | 0 | 2 | 1 |
| Classrooms and assembly areas | 0 | 5 | 4 |
| Playgrounds | 1 | 3 | 2 |
| **Total** | **4** | **52** | **34** |

Notable district-wide trends include:

1. **Door opening force:** Several interior doors were measured at 6–8 lbf, exceeding the 5 lbf maximum. Most affected doors are in older buildings with hydraulic closers that have not been adjusted since installation.
2. **Restroom signage:** A number of single-user restrooms lack tactile signage or have signs mounted at incorrect heights. This was the most common Code 2 deficiency.
3. **Path-of-travel obstructions:** Three sites had temporary obstructions (e.g., stored furniture, custodial carts) in accessible routes. These were resolved on-site during inspections or escalated as Code 1 findings.
4. **Playground surfacing:** One playground had a section of rubber tile surfacing with a raised edge, creating a trip hazard and a potential barrier for wheelchair users.

documents.content:
Cedar Ridge Elementary School is a single-story campus constructed in 1978, with a classroom addition completed in 2004. The site serves approximately 480 students in grades K–5. The main building houses administrative offices, a library, and 18 classrooms. A separate building contains the multi-purpose room and a small kitchen. The school has one main entrance on Cedar Ridge Road and a secondary entrance on the east side of the campus that opens onto the parent drop-off loop.

---

**Parking and Passenger Loading**

The main parking lot contains 42 standard spaces, 5 accessible parking spaces, and 2 van-accessible spaces. The accessible spaces are located directly adjacent to the main entrance walkway, on the north side of the lot. The van-accessible spaces are striped with a 96-inch access aisle. All accessible spaces are marked with the International Symbol of Accessibility and are posted with a "Van Accessible" sign where applicable. The access aisles are level and free of cracks, and the painted striping is in good condition with no evidence of fading. The slope of the parking lot at the accessible spaces measures 1.5%, which is within the 2.0% maximum allowable cross slope.

---

**Exterior Routes and Ramps**

The primary accessible route from the parking lot to the main entrance is a 5-foot-wide concrete walkway. The walkway surface is in good condition with no cracks or vertical discontinuities exceeding 1/4 inch. The route passes through a gate that provides a clear opening width of 36 inches.

A secondary route on the east side of the campus connects the drop-off loop to the multi-purpose room. This route includes a ramp with a running slope of 6.2%, a landing at the top measuring 5 feet by 5 feet, and handrails on both sides at a height of 34 inches. The handrails are continuous and have a return to the wall at the bottom. No deficiencies were noted on this route.

Cedar Ridge Elementary School has_accessible_parking_spaces 5 spaces. Record status: current.

---

**Entrances and Doorways**

The main entrance features a power-operated door with a push-button actuator mounted at 36 inches above the floor. The door provides a clear opening width of 40 inches. The actuator is labeled with the International Symbol of Accessibility and is in working order. The door opening force was measured at 4.5 lbf, which is within the 5 lbf maximum.

The east entrance, used for the drop-off loop, has a manual door with a clear opening width of 34 inches. The door opening force was measured at 6.5 lbf, exceeding the 5 lbf maximum. This was noted as a Code 2 deficiency. The door closer is a standard hydraulic unit that appears to have been installed in 2004 and has not been adjusted since that time. Corrective action is required within 180 days.

The multi-purpose room entrance has a double-door assembly with one leaf fixed and one leaf operable. The operable leaf provides a clear opening width of 32 inches. The threshold is beveled and measures 1/2 inch in height. No deficiencies were noted at this entrance.

---

**Restrooms**

The main building has two single-user restrooms designated as accessible, located adjacent to the administrative office. Each restroom is equipped with a toilet, a lavatory, and a mirror. The toilet is positioned with the centerline 18 inches from the side wall, and the seat height measures 17 inches. Grab bars are installed on the side wall and the rear wall, each measuring 42 inches in length and mounted at 33 inches above the floor. The lavatory has a clear knee space measuring 29 inches high, 30 inches wide, and 11 inches deep. The faucet is a single-lever type with a 5-second shutoff.

**Fairview Unified School District Accessibility Compliance Report – 2026**

---

**Section 3: District-Wide Recommendations**

The following recommendations are offered to the Board, the Superintendent, and school administrators based on the findings of the January and February 2026 inspections. These recommendations are organized by category and are intended to guide the district’s capital improvement planning, maintenance scheduling, and budget requests for the 2026–27 fiscal year.

---

**3.1 Door Openings and Hardware**

Manual door opening forces exceeding the 5 lbf maximum were the single most common deficiency noted across the district, appearing at eleven of the fourteen schools inspected. In most cases, the measured force fell between 5.5 and 7.0 lbf, indicating that the door closers are set too high or have drifted out of adjustment over time. The district should direct Maintenance & Operations (M&O) to perform a systematic adjustment of door closers at all school entrances, administrative offices, and restrooms. Where adjustment does not bring the force within the 5 lbf maximum, the closer should be replaced. This work can be completed by in-house staff and does not require outside contractors. The Accessibility Services Office (ASO) will re-test any door repaired under this recommendation within 60 days of the work order being closed.

The district should also adopt a standard specification for all new door hardware purchases: lever handles, no knobs; opening force not to exceed 5 lbf; and automatic door operators on all main public entrances. The current practice of installing manual doors at new construction sites has contributed to the recurring force violations.

---

**3.2 Drinking Fountains**

The inspection found drinking fountains with spout heights above the 36-inch maximum at six schools. In each case, the fountain was a wall-mounted unit with a manual push-button actuator. The district should prioritize replacement of these units with accessible, hands-free models. For the 2026–27 budget cycle, ASO recommends that the district allocate funds to replace at least four of the six non-compliant fountains, beginning with those located in gymnasium lobbies and student common areas where usage is highest. The remaining two fountains should be replaced in the following fiscal year.

While replacement is pending, M&O should post a temporary sign at each non-compliant fountain directing users to the nearest accessible fountain. The sign should include the location of the accessible unit and should be mounted at 48 to 60 inches above the floor.

---

**3.3 Restroom Facilities**

The most significant restroom issue identified during the inspections was at Lincoln Elementary School, where the accessible restroom in the kindergarten wing did not have a properly functioning emergency call button. The call button at that location was not connected to the main office and produced no signal when tested. This was classified as a Code 1 deficiency and was corrected on February 9, 2026, by M&O. The district should review the monthly testing log for all emergency call buttons to ensure that testing is actually being performed and documented. ASO recommends that the testing log be maintained at each school's main office and that the principal or designee initial the log after each monthly test.

The district should also evaluate the mounting height of toilet paper dispensers in accessible stalls. While the dispensers inspected were all within reach range, several were mounted at 24 inches above the floor, which is the minimum acceptable height but is not comfortable for all users. ASO recommends that new dispensers be mounted at 26 to 28 inches above the floor, and that M&O adjust existing dispensers when they are replaced.

**3.4 Drinking Fountains (continued) – Cedar Ridge Elementary School**

During the February 3, 2026 inspection of Cedar Ridge Elementary School, ASO staff reviewed the drinking fountains in all occupied wings and the gymnasium lobby. The school has a total of eight drinking fountains. Six are accessible units with both a standard and a lower-height basin. Two are older wall-mounted units with a single basin and a manual push-button actuator.

The two single-basin units are located in the gymnasium lobby and in the corridor outside the music room. Both units have the basin rim mounted at 34 inches above the floor, which is within the required reach range. However, the push-button actuator on the gymnasium lobby unit requires 6.5 pounds of force to activate, exceeding the 5-pound maximum permitted under the current standards. The actuator on the music room unit requires 5.25 pounds of force, also above the maximum. Both units were classified as Code 2 deficiencies because they do not prevent use of the facility, but they do not provide equal access for all users.

The remaining six fountains, including the accessible units in the kindergarten wing and the upper-grade corridor, were found to be in compliance. The accessible units have a clear floor space of 30 inches by 48 inches in front of the basin, and the basin rim is mounted at 32 to 34 inches above the floor. The push-button actuators on these units require 3 to 4 pounds of force and are mounted on the front of the basin. No temporary signage was needed at Cedar Ridge because the two non-compliant units are located within 50 feet of a compliant accessible unit in the same corridor or lobby.

M&O has been issued a work order to adjust the actuator tension on both single-basin units. The work order, M&O-2026-0317, was created on February 5, 2026, and is scheduled for completion by February 27, 2026. If the actuator cannot be adjusted to fall within the 5-pound maximum, the units should be replaced with hands-free models. ASO will re-inspect both locations after the work order is marked complete.

**3.5 Parking and Passenger Loading Zones – Cedar Ridge Elementary School**

The parking lot at Cedar Ridge Elementary School has 142 standard parking spaces and 6 accessible spaces. The accessible spaces are located at the north end of the lot, adjacent to the main entrance walkway. All six accessible spaces have the required 8-foot access aisle, and the access aisles are marked with blue paint and the international symbol of accessibility. The surface of the lot is asphalt and was found to be in good condition, with no cracks or potholes that would impede travel.

The van-accessible space at the north end of the lot has a 5-foot vertical clearance, which is below the 8-foot 2-inch minimum required for van-accessible spaces. The clearance is limited by the branch of a mature oak tree that overhangs the space. This was classified as a Code 2 deficiency. The tree is maintained by the Grounds Department, and ASO has requested that the branch be pruned to provide the required clearance. The pruning is scheduled to be completed by March 15, 2026, before the spring planting season begins.

The other five accessible spaces have no vertical clearance issues. The access aisle for each of these spaces is flush with the parking surface and connects directly to the curb ramp. The curb ramp at the north end of the lot has a slope of 1:12 and a flared side with a slope of 1:10, both within the acceptable range. The ramp surface is concrete with a broom finish and was found to be free of cracks and chips.

documents.content:
**3.6 Gymnasium and Elevator – Westbrook Middle School**

The gymnasium at Westbrook Middle School is the primary indoor physical education facility for the school and is also used for community events after hours. The gymnasium has two main public entrances: one at the east side, off the main corridor, and one at the west side, adjacent to the locker rooms. Both entrances are equipped with double doors. The east entrance has a power-operated door opener on the left leaf, which was tested during the inspection and found to be functioning within the required 5-second opening and closing cycle. The west entrance has no power-operated opener; the door is a manual double set with a combined opening force of 8.5 pounds, which exceeds the 5-pound maximum for interior doors. This was classified as a Code 2 deficiency. M&O has been issued a work order, M&O-2026-0341, created on February 10, 2026, to install a power-operated door opener on the west entrance. The work order is scheduled for completion by March 20, 2026. ASO will re-inspect the west entrance after the work order is marked complete.

Inside the gymnasium, the main floor is a hardwood surface with a slip-resistant finish. The surface was found to be in good condition, with no warping, splinters, or uneven transitions. The basketball court lines are painted and in good condition. The gymnasium also has a stage at the north end, which is used for assemblies and performances. The stage is elevated 24 inches above the gymnasium floor. There is no ramp or lift providing access to the stage. The only means of access is a stairway with three steps at the west side of the stage. The stairway has a handrail on one side, which is within the required height range of 34 to 38 inches. The lack of an accessible route to the stage was classified as a Code 1 deficiency, as the stage is a program area that must be accessible. ASO has recommended that a portable ramp be acquired and stored in the gymnasium equipment room. The ramp should have a slope of 1:12 or less and a minimum clear width of 36 inches. A request for quote has been sent to three vendors, and ASO expects to have a recommendation by March 5, 2026.

The gymnasium also has a public address system and a scoreboard mounted on the east wall. The scoreboard controls are located at the scorer's table, which is at floor level and accessible. The PA system controls are in a locked cabinet at the north end of the gymnasium, behind the stage. The cabinet is at a height of 48 inches above the floor, which is within the accessible reach range of 15 to 48 inches. The cabinet lock was operable with a standard key, and the controls were found to be in good working order.

The elevator at Westbrook Middle School is located in the main lobby, adjacent to the school office. The elevator provides access to all three floors of the building. The elevator car has a clear width of 42 inches and a clear depth of 54 inches, which meets the minimum dimensions for a standard accessible elevator. The car door has a clear opening of 36 inches. The elevator was inspected on February 12, 2026. The car leveling was tested and found to be within 0.5 inches of the floor landing at all three stops. The door opening and closing time was measured at 4 seconds, which is within the required range. The elevator car has a handrail on the back wall, which is mounted at a height of 34 inches. The handrail is in good condition, with no loose or missing brackets.
